C2: NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup point, and the platform separately recorded arrival at 09:02:40. [F6 F5] [NS-1]
C3: NS-1(ii) is satisfied: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 39 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius; the same 39 m distance is recorded for the whole stationary period. [F6 F3] [NS-1]
C4: NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record: after the 09:03:00 tap the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup continuously for 6 min 10 s until the rider's own cancellation at 09:09:10, and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 6 min 30 s — both well over 3 min 1 s. [F6 F3 F2] [NS-1]

claims.assertion: This is an immediate booking (RydeX) cancelled by the rider 9 min 0 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand if NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all met; the burden of those three elements is on the record, and each must be checked.
NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup point, and the platform separately recorded arrival at 09:02:40.

NS-1(ii) is satisfied: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 39 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius; the same 39 m distance is recorded for the whole stationary period.

NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record: after the 09:03:00 tap the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup continuously for 6 min 10 s until the rider's own cancellation at 09:09:10, and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 6 min 30 s — both well over 3 min 1 s.

The rider's own messages confirm the delay was hers, not the driver's: at 09:05 she wrote "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" and she does not dispute that she was still upstairs when she cancelled at 09:09:10.

There is no evidence gap that would push this to manual review: the chat record is complete with 3 timestamped messages, and the GPS track covers the stationary period right through to the cancellation moment with no gap alleged.

Ryde publishes no rule that a driver arriving late, or that the rider being only a couple of minutes away, waives the $6.61 fee; the rider's remedy is a discretionary appeal rather than an entitlement, and the voucher-based refund of $6.61 is the form any relief would take.

weaknesses: NS-1's third element is met on the system records the other side will rely on: F3 and F6 show a single uninterrupted 6 min 10 s stationary period at 39 m from pickup immediately after the tap, and F2 shows 6 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m — I cannot point to any gap or contradiction that breaks the '> 3 min' condition.

The rider's own message F10 ("Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" at 09:05) is a written admission that she was not at the pickup point and did not arrive, which the driver will pair with F11 ("Waited 5 min already") and F13 to defeat any argument that the driver failed to wait or was uncontactable.

My client's own account (she got held up and gave up) and her profile, F17 (3 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld), give the driver an unreasonableness narrative, and F18 (700 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) removes any basis for attacking the driver's credibility or seeking flag_account.

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
D1: This is a rider-cancelled immediate booking: the rider accepted at 09:00:10 and cancelled at 09:09:10, which is 9 min 0 s after matching and therefore well past the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee stands. [F4] [NS-0 NS-4]
D2: The driver satisfied every element of the no-show test: the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 with the driver 39 m from the pickup point, and the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m arrival radius. [F5 F6 F1] [NS-1]
D3: After the "I'm Here" tap the driver remained continuously within 200 m of the pickup point for 6 min 10 s until the rider cancelled at 09:09:10 — more than double the 3-minute threshold — so requirement (iii) of NS-1 is met; the GPS corroborates a single stationary period 09:03:00–09:09:10 at 39 m from the pickup. [F6 F3 F2 F4] [NS-1]
D4: Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all satisfied, cancellation fee $6.61 is properly charged and the correct outcome for the driver is no_action, leaving the $6.61 (of which $4.50 is the driver's share) undisturbed. [F4 F7 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
D5: The rider's own message at 09:05 confirms she had not arrived and was still "2 more minutes" away, and the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped, so nothing in the record rebuts the driver's account or suggests late arrival. [F10 F12 F9] [NS-1]
D6: The driver's own contemporaneous message and written statement — "Waited 5 min already" and "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" — are consistent with, and corroborated by, the GPS stationary period of 6 min 10 s, so no adverse inference of the driver cancelling early or leaving arises. [F11 F13 F3] [NS-1]
D7: The rider's account is 300 days old with 3 disputes in 90 d and a 4.5 rating, while the driver has 1,600 days, 700 trips in 90 d, a 4.9 rating and 0 disputes/0 upheld — this pattern supports declining a refund as a courtesy; the profile facts are offered only as supporting weight, not as the basis of the finding. [F17 F18] [NS-1]
D8: No safety issue arises: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint contains a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so the fare question can be decided on the record rather than escalated. [F9 F10 F11 F13] [SAFE-1 SAFE-2]
Weaknesses: The rider's complaint says she "told the driver I was two minutes away, then got held up" — the 09:05 chat (F10) supports that she was a few minutes away and did try to come down, so the judge may read the record sympathetically and view a $6.61 charge on a 9-minute wait as harsh; however NS-4/NS-1 give no discretion for a good excuse. | The fee is charged to the rider's account as $6.61 (F7), so if the judge is inclined toward goodwill under the voucher mechanism in NS-7 the platform could waive it; my client rejects that on NS-1 grounds, but the discretionary refund power in NS-7 is acknowledged. | The driver never sent a message between 09:05 and 09:08 (F10, F11), so the rider could argue the driver did not warn that the 3-minute no-show window had expired before cancelling — the policy imposes no such warning duty (NS-1 requires only arrival, position within 200 m and >3 minutes of continuous waiting, all shown by F2/F3/F5/F6), but the fact gap is the strongest point the other side can press. | The arrival radius used (200 m, F6 at 39 m) is a data-layer parameter pending Ryde confirmation (G2), so the rider could faintly argue the arrival determination should be measured differently; the 39 m figure comfortably satisfies any plausible radius.
Asks: no_action

claims.assertion: This is a rider-cancelled immediate booking: the rider accepted at 09:00:10 and cancelled at 09:09:10, which is 9 min 0 s after matching and therefore well past the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee stands.

The driver satisfied every element of the no-show test: the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 with the driver 39 m from the pickup point, and the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m arrival radius.

After the "I'm Here" tap the driver remained continuously within 200 m of the pickup point for 6 min 10 s until the rider cancelled at 09:09:10 — more than double the 3-minute threshold — so requirement (iii) of NS-1 is met; the GPS corroborates a single stationary period 09:03:00–09:09:10 at 39 m from the pickup.

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all satisfied, cancellation fee $6.61 is properly charged and the correct outcome for the driver is no_action, leaving the $6.61 (of which $4.50 is the driver's share) undisturbed.

The rider's own message at 09:05 confirms she had not arrived and was still "2 more minutes" away, and the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped, so nothing in the record rebuts the driver's account or suggests late arrival.

The driver's own contemporaneous message and written statement — "Waited 5 min already" and "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" — are consistent with, and corroborated by, the GPS stationary period of 6 min 10 s, so no adverse inference of the driver cancelling early or leaving arises.

The rider's account is 300 days old with 3 disputes in 90 d and a 4.5 rating, while the driver has 1,600 days, 700 trips in 90 d, a 4.9 rating and 0 disputes/0 upheld — this pattern supports declining a refund as a courtesy; the profile facts are offered only as supporting weight, not as the basis of the finding.

No safety issue arises: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint contains a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so the fare question can be decided on the record rather than escalated.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint says she "told the driver I was two minutes away, then got held up" — the 09:05 chat (F10) supports that she was a few minutes away and did try to come down, so the judge may read the record sympathetically and view a $6.61 charge on a 9-minute wait as harsh; however NS-4/NS-1 give no discretion for a good excuse.

The fee is charged to the rider's account as $6.61 (F7), so if the judge is inclined toward goodwill under the voucher mechanism in NS-7 the platform could waive it; my client rejects that on NS-1 grounds, but the discretionary refund power in NS-7 is acknowledged.

The driver never sent a message between 09:05 and 09:08 (F10, F11), so the rider could argue the driver did not warn that the 3-minute no-show window had expired before cancelling — the policy imposes no such warning duty (NS-1 requires only arrival, position within 200 m and >3 minutes of continuous waiting, all shown by F2/F3/F5/F6), but the fact gap is the strongest point the other side can press.

The arrival radius used (200 m, F6 at 39 m) is a data-layer parameter pending Ryde confirmation (G2), so the rider could faintly argue the arrival determination should be measured differently; the 39 m figure comfortably satisfies any plausible radius.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This is an immediate booking (RydeX) cancelled by the rider 9 min 0 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand if NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all met; the burden of those three elements is on the record, and each must be checked.
NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup point, and the platform separately recorded arrival at 09:02:40.

NS-1(ii) is satisfied: at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 39 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius; the same 39 m distance is recorded for the whole stationary period.

NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record: after the 09:03:00 tap the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup continuously for 6 min 10 s until the rider's own cancellation at 09:09:10, and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 6 min 30 s — both well over 3 min 1 s.

The rider's own messages confirm the delay was hers, not the driver's: at 09:05 she wrote "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" and she does not dispute that she was still upstairs when she cancelled at 09:09:10.

There is no evidence gap that would push this to manual review: the chat record is complete with 3 timestamped messages, and the GPS track covers the stationary period right through to the cancellation moment with no gap alleged.

Ryde publishes no rule that a driver arriving late, or that the rider being only a couple of minutes away, waives the $6.61 fee; the rider's remedy is a discretionary appeal rather than an entitlement, and the voucher-based refund of $6.61 is the form any relief would take.

weaknesses: NS-1's third element is met on the system records the other side will rely on: F3 and F6 show a single uninterrupted 6 min 10 s stationary period at 39 m from pickup immediately after the tap, and F2 shows 6 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m — I cannot point to any gap or contradiction that breaks the '> 3 min' condition.

The rider's own message F10 ("Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" at 09:05) is a written admission that she was not at the pickup point and did not arrive, which the driver will pair with F11 ("Waited 5 min already") and F13 to defeat any argument that the driver failed to wait or was uncontactable.

My client's own account (she got held up and gave up) and her profile, F17 (3 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld), give the driver an unreasonableness narrative, and F18 (700 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) removes any basis for attacking the driver's credibility or seeking flag_account.
The cancellation fee is $6.61 as recorded in F7 with no surge (F8), so any partial-refund arithmetic is unavailable — the outcome is binary full refund or no_action.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-cancelled immediate booking: the rider accepted at 09:00:10 and cancelled at 09:09:10, which is 9 min 0 s after matching and therefore well past the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee stands.

The driver satisfied every element of the no-show test: the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 with the driver 39 m from the pickup point, and the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m arrival radius.

After the "I'm Here" tap the driver remained continuously within 200 m of the pickup point for 6 min 10 s until the rider cancelled at 09:09:10 — more than double the 3-minute threshold — so requirement (iii) of NS-1 is met; the GPS corroborates a single stationary period 09:03:00–09:09:10 at 39 m from the pickup.

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are all satisfied, cancellation fee $6.61 is properly charged and the correct outcome for the driver is no_action, leaving the $6.61 (of which $4.50 is the driver's share) undisturbed.

The rider's own message at 09:05 confirms she had not arrived and was still "2 more minutes" away, and the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped, so nothing in the record rebuts the driver's account or suggests late arrival.

The driver's own contemporaneous message and written statement — "Waited 5 min already" and "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice" — are consistent with, and corroborated by, the GPS stationary period of 6 min 10 s, so no adverse inference of the driver cancelling early or leaving arises.

The rider's account is 300 days old with 3 disputes in 90 d and a 4.5 rating, while the driver has 1,600 days, 700 trips in 90 d, a 4.9 rating and 0 disputes/0 upheld — this pattern supports declining a refund as a courtesy; the profile facts are offered only as supporting weight, not as the basis of the finding.

No safety issue arises: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint contains a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so the fare question can be decided on the record rather than escalated.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint says she "told the driver I was two minutes away, then got held up" — the 09:05 chat (F10) supports that she was a few minutes away and did try to come down, so the judge may read the record sympathetically and view a $6.61 charge on a 9-minute wait as harsh; however NS-4/NS-1 give no discretion for a good excuse.

The fee is charged to the rider's account as $6.61 (F7), so if the judge is inclined toward goodwill under the voucher mechanism in NS-7 the platform could waive it; my client rejects that on NS-1 grounds, but the discretionary refund power in NS-7 is acknowledged.

The driver never sent a message between 09:05 and 09:08 (F10, F11), so the rider could argue the driver did not warn that the 3-minute no-show window had expired before cancelling — the policy imposes no such warning duty (NS-1 requires only arrival, position within 200 m and >3 minutes of continuous waiting, all shown by F2/F3/F5/F6), but the fact gap is the strongest point the other side can press.

The arrival radius used (200 m, F6 at 39 m) is a data-layer parameter pending Ryde confirmation (G2), so the rider could faintly argue the arrival determination should be measured differently; the 39 m figure comfortably satisfies any plausible radius.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance (F4), so NS-4's 3-minute free window does not help, and any relief must come from NS-7's discretionary voucher review, not NS-4 — my brief already framed it that way in C7.
Conceded: (i) and (ii) are on the record — platform arrival at 09:02:40 (F5) and the driver's own tap at 09:03:00 while 39 m from pickup (F6), inside any plausible arrival radius.

Conceded: the continuous stationary period 09:03:00–09:09:10 at 39 m (F3), 6 min 10 s after the tap (F6) and 6 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m (F2), satisfies NS-1(iii) — I have no fact that breaks the continuity or shows the driver leaving.

I do not contest that on NS-1/N S-4 the fee is technically chargeable and the formal outcome is no_action; I note only that NS-7 preserves Ryde's discretion to issue a $6.61 voucher, which is the whole of what my client asks for (F7).

I accept F10 is my client's own message and that it defeats any no-show defence; I rely on it only as evidence that she was engaged and coming down, while conceding that the wait still exceeded the policy threshold (F10, F4).

The driver's messages and statement are consistent with the GPS and I do not allege early departure or uncontactability (F11, F13, F3); the only point left is that nothing in NS-1 required the driver to warn the rider before the window expired, and I do not press otherwise.

Profile facts cannot decide the case and cut both ways: my client's F17 (300 d, rating 4.5, 0 upheld) and the driver's F18 (0 disputes, 0 upheld) show no pattern of abuse on either side, so neither supports denying a one-off discretionary voucher.

Agreed there is no safety trigger: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation arises (F9, F10, F11, F13).

I withdraw nothing but tighten my ask: I do not seek a reversal under NS-1/N S-4, only the discretionary $6.61 voucher under NS-7, and I note for completeness that no traffic or weather excuse exists on either side of this fare question (F14, F15, F16).

Agreed on the framing: NS-0 routes this rider-cancelled immediate booking into NS-4, and NS-4 is satisfied because the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance (F4), well past both the 3-minute free-cancellation and the 3-minute no-show windows; the NS-1 elements are independently met as conceded below.
Conceded — F6 records the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 09:03:00 at 39 m from the pickup point, and F5 records the platform arrival at 09:02:40; nothing on my side disputes that NS-1(i) is met.

Conceded — F6 places the driver 39 m from the pickup point at the moment of the tap, far inside the 200 m arrival radius, and F3 shows the identical 39 m position across the stationary period; NS-1(ii) is satisfied on the system records.

Conceded — after the 09:03:00 tap (F6) the driver held position 39 m from pickup for the single uninterrupted stationary period 09:03:00–09:09:10 (F3) and accumulated 6 min 30 s within 200 m before the rider cancelled (F2, F4), i.e. more than double the 3 min 1 s threshold in NS-1(iii).

Adopted as supporting the driver: the rider's 09:05 message "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" (F10) is a written admission at 09:05 that she had still not reached the Tanjong Pagar Centre stand the driver had announced at 09:03 (F9), and she then cancelled at 09:09:10 (F4) — the failure to arrive was hers and lasted past both windows.

Adopted — F12 shows a complete chat record of 3 timestamped messages and F3/F2 show the GPS covering the whole wait through to 09:09:10, so there is no G12-type evidence gap and no reason to send the case to manual review; the driver's statement (F13) is extra colour, not a substitute for records.

Adopted with one clarification: because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are all met (F5, F6, F3, F2), the $6.61 charge (F7) is a valid charge rather than a discretionary grace case, so the voucher mechanism in NS-7 has nothing to refund and NS-4 requires no_action; no rule allowing waiver merely because a rider is two minutes away exists in the policy.
